rationale: Seven defects: two parser crashes on invalid input (non-array argument and non-string elements), confirm-kind message leaks raw (Y/n) hint text confirmed by the activate.json recording, an overly broad '(' prefix filter silently drops valid options, and last-of-multiple selection markers wins rather than first; in the recording tool, a >20-char heuristic misses short credential prompts and recursive next() overflows the stack on large recordings. No spec existed; blind and verification-gap lenses are n/a for the compact profile. One finding dismissed (30-element viewport limit; JSDoc-documented contract enforced by the driver's readScreen).

findings.title: Non-string element crashes detectPrompt
findings.problem: isQ(l) calls l.trimStart() with no type guard. A null, undefined, or numeric element anywhere in the lines array causes a TypeError on that iteration.
findings.impact: The parse aborts mid-scan and detectPrompt throws instead of returning null, crashing the caller.
findings.recommendation: Add a type guard: const isQ = (l) => typeof l === 'string' && l.trimStart().startsWith('?');

findings.title: No array-type guard crashes on null input
findings.problem: detectPrompt(lines) accesses lines.length with no Array.isArray guard. A null, undefined, or non-array argument throws TypeError before any parsing begins.
findings.impact: Caller crashes; detectPrompt never returns, halting the setup driver.
findings.recommendation: Add if (!Array.isArray(lines)) return null; at the top of detectPrompt.

findings.title: Confirm message includes raw hint text
findings.problem: For confirm-kind prompts (activate, installClaude) the message is built by stripping only the leading '?' from the line; the trailing '(Y/n)' or '(y/N)' suffix is not removed. The activate.json recording confirms the live line ends with '(Y/n)': '? Switch to profile "anthropic-subscription" as active? (Y/n) '.
findings.impact: Callers receive messages like 'Switch to profile ... (Y/n)' or 'Would you like to install Claude Code now? (Y/n)' instead of clean prompt text; any UI layer displaying or logging the message gets the raw hint artifact.
findings.recommendation: Strip the confirm hint after building the message for confirm-kind entries: message = message.replace(/\s*\(y\/[nN]\)\s*$|\s*\([yY]\/n\)\s*$/i, '').trim();

findings.title: Paren-start filter silently drops valid list options
findings.problem: if (t.startsWith('(')) continue; skips every trimmed option line that begins with '('. The intent is to skip the '(Use arrow keys)' and '(Move up and down...)' hint lines, but the filter is over-broad and will match any option whose label starts with a parenthesis.
findings.impact: An option like '(beta) model-name' or '(free tier) provider' is silently excluded from the returned options list; the driver sees fewer options than are on screen. Reachability is uncertain against current fixtures but the filter is structurally incorrect.
findings.recommendation: Replace with explicit hint-text matches: if (/^\(Use arrow keys\)/i.test(t) || /^\(Move up and down/i.test(t)) continue;

findings.title: Last selection marker wins on multi-marker screens
findings.problem: if (sel) selectedIndex = options.length; unconditionally overwrites selectedIndex for every '>' or '\u276f' marked row. In a partial terminal render with multiple markers (a transient state possible at 256-byte chunk boundaries), the last marked row is returned as the selection, not the first (cursor position).
findings.impact: selectedIndex misreports the current selection; the driver highlights the wrong option. Reachability is uncertain — normal renders carry one marker — but partial-render multi-marker states are possible during chunk-boundary writes.
findings.recommendation: Record only the first selection marker: introduce a seenSel boolean flag and skip subsequent sel=true assignments once seenSel is true.

findings.title: Short credential prompts never captured
findings.problem: promptId returns 'credential' only when line.trim().length > 20. A credential prompt label of 20 characters or fewer (e.g., '? API key: ' is 11 chars) returns null, so no fixture is written for that prompt.
findings.impact: Any provider whose credential prompt text is short never has a fixture captured by this tool, leaving that prompt undetected and untested.
findings.recommendation: Remove the length heuristic and rely solely on snapped.has('provider') as the false-positive guard: inside that branch, return 'credential' for any question line regardless of length.

findings.title: Recursive next() overflows stack on large recordings
findings.problem: Each 256-byte chunk calls next() recursively from inside the term.write callback. For a ~10 MB TypeScript recording (~40 000 chunks), the synchronous recursion depth exceeds Node.js's default stack limit (~10 000 frames) and throws RangeError.
findings.impact: The recording tool crashes mid-capture on large session files, leaving fixture files incomplete or absent.
findings.recommendation: Replace the recursive next() call with setImmediate(next) to yield to the event loop between chunks, making traversal iterative.
